spots.chart_note: Top: the fishing score through the day; green = a window (fishable, Good or better), red = can't be fished. Bottom: blue = falling water, as depth at the dock. Dotted line = 1 ft (too shallow below). Shaded columns = rain chance (darker = likelier; purple = storms). Bottom strip shows night, twilight and daylight.
spots.rules_text: The chart scores every 15 minutes from first light to last light: falling water, up to 70 points at 0.5 ft/h or more (rising water earns 60% of that), plus up to 30 for light (full from first light to 60 min after sunrise and from 60 min before sunset to last light, none by midday). Points lost: chop from the wind: moderate chop (13–17 mph) −10, choppy (18–23 mph) −25, rough (over 23 mph) −40; SSW–WSW wind counts one step rougher; murky water (wind averaging 13 mph or more over the 12 h before) −10 (not on top of chop); rain chance 20%+ −5, 50%+ −10; storms −20; cool water (under 60°) −10. Wind on its own costs nothing. Heights are depth at the dock: under 1 ft it can't be fished (score at most 25), under 0.5 ft it scores 0. Grades: Prime 90+, Great 75+, Good 60+, Fair 40+, Poor below; Prime also needs nothing lost but water speed or light. A window is a fishable stretch of 30+ minutes scoring 60+, graded on its best 60 minutes. Red tide nearby or cold water (under 55°) is Skip. Water temperature and red tide use the latest reading for every day.
